text:
Irene: quick idea for discussion: introduce a "resident shadow proxy" concept to reduce accidental cross-region KV writes during brief failovers and to keep routing decisions auditable. thoughts?

Ben: what's a resident shadow proxy in 1 line?

Irene: a lightweight edge component that holds per-tenant residency decision logs and answers proxy routing queries locally instead of always hitting control-plane. it would say: "route-to: eu-west-1, policy: prefer-local, reason: recent-lease-swap".

Sasha: sounds like a cache of the control-plane residency state. main concerns: staleness and token-sync.

Irene: agreed. plan is: 1) residency decisions are signed by control-plane (small token), 2) shadow proxies validate signature and serve queries for TTL, 3) on lease-swap control-plane pushes signed delta so shadows sync quickly.

Juniper: what problems does this solve vs current proxy+control-plane?

Irene: mostly two pain points: a) reduces control-plane control calls on every request which reduces token issuance churn during flaps, b) provides an audit trail close to the edge so we can prove why a write was allowed in a region.

Ben: show me the proto you imagine for the proxy call.

Irene: rough header idea:

```
X-Residency-Decision: region=eu-west-1;policy=prefer;epoch=512;sig=base64
X-Decision-Src: shadow-proxy-id=asn-42
```

Sasha: verification steps in dataplane?

Irene: dataplane checks signature -> checks epoch vs local lease watermark -> if policy==strict && region!=resident -> reject 409, else allow per policy. Shadow proxies return the full signed decision to the dataplane.

Juniper: telemetry/ops asks: we need shadow-sync-lag, decision-cache-hit, percent-decisions-signed-by-shadow, and decision-rejects-by-policy. add a dashboard for shadow health.

Ben: compliance: signed decision logs are helpful but we must ensure logs are immutable and exported for legal holds. shadow proxies should push an append-only audit stream to the central audit store.

Sasha: security: what keys sign decisions? per-tenant or regional control-plane key? per-tenant is ideal but key proliferation is a pain. maybe per-tenant derived keys (signed by control-plane master) + short TTL.

Irene: exactly. derivation approach: control-plane signs a small KDF token per tenant with expiry. shadow proxies verify using the derived key. we rotate master keys centrally.

Juniper: what about the risk that a compromised shadow proxy issues stale/incorrect decisions?

Irene: mitigation: dataplane must check decision signatures against control-plane KDF public material; plus we'll add a heartbeat: decisions include a monotonic sequence number and shadow proxies must publish periodic signed checkpoints to control-plane. any gap triggers fail-to-strict fallback.

Ben: ops controls: add a global kill-switch so we can disable shadow-decisions and fallback to control-plane-only routing. Also allow per-tenant opt-out.

Sasha: test plan: simulate heavy control-plane flaps, force-shadow-desync, and verify dataplane rejects stale decisions. also run compliance export tests to ensure shadow logs are exportable.

Irene: performance note: shadow proxies only store tiny decision tuples, not full tenant state. memory/lightweight. goal <1ms decision lookup for forwarded requests.

Juniper: SDKs need new error mapping: if dataplane rejects with epoch mismatch include `X-Resident-Epoch` hint so clients can rebind. also surface a `ShadowDecisionMismatch` metric.

ops-bot: created ticket ARCH-9421: resident-shadow-proxy + signed-decisions + audit-stream + telemetry.

Ben: potential rollout: start with read-only decisions in staging, then allow idempotent writes under shadow-decisions in canary, then full write support per-tenant. include kill-switch in each step.

Sasha: agree. add automatic throttling: if shadow-decisions error-rate > 1% flip to control-plane routing for that region.

Irene: next steps: I'll draft an RFC that includes decision token format, shadow sync protocol, audit-stream schema, and rollback steps. will ping security/ops/compliance for review.

Juniper: +1. I'll help with sequence-number invariants and checkpointing tests.

Ben: +1. will own rollout plan and canary metrics.

Irene: thanks all. will drop RFC link when ready. :pray:
